Or he is a mercy for the believers, since he rescued them from disbelief to faith, and intercedes for them in the Hereafter on account of their faith in this world. ﴿And those who harm the Messenger of Allah, for them is a painful punishment﴾ in both abodes.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 62:

﴿They swear by Allah to you, to please you.﴾ The address is to the Muslims. The hypocrites (munafiqun) would speak disparagingly (bi-l-mata'in), or would stay behind from the jihad, then come to them and offer excuses to them, and they would reinforce their excuses with oaths, so that they would accept their excuses and be pleased with them. So it was said to them: ﴿Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should be pleased, if they are believers.﴾ That is: if you are believers as you claim, then the one most deserving that you please with obedience and agreement is Allah and His Messenger. He used the singular pronoun (wahhada al-damir) because there is no difference between the pleasure of Allah and the pleasure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); the two are in the ruling of one thing, like your saying: "The kindness of Zayd and his generosity (ijmaluhu) has supported me (na'ashani)." Or: "Allah has more right that they should be pleased, and His Messenger likewise."

Do they not know that ﴿whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger﴾ — أنَّ الأمْرَ والشَأْنَ (that the matter and affair is this) — exceeds the limit through opposition. It is a *mufā'alah* (the verbal form III pattern, مُفاعَلَةٌ) from *al-ḥadd* (the limit, الحَدّ), like *al-mushāqqah* (opposition, المُشاقَّةِ) from *al-shaqq* (splitting, الشَقّ).

﴿Then indeed for him﴾ is with the predicate (الخَبَر, *khabar*) omitted, i.e., "then it is certain that for him ﴿the fire of Hell, abiding therein; that is the great disgrace.﴾"

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 64:

﴿The hypocrites are wary﴾: this is a statement with the meaning of a command, i.e., let the hypocrites be wary ﴿lest a surah be sent down concerning them﴾. (Tunazzala) with the lightened form (tanzil): this is the reading of Makki and Basri.

﴿It informs them of what is in their hearts﴾ of disbelief and hypocrisy. The pronouns refer to the hypocrites, because when a surah is sent down concerning their situation, it is as though it is sent down upon them. The proof of this is the verse ﴿Say: "Mock, [if you will]"﴾. Or the first two (pronouns) refer to the believers and the third to the hypocrites, and this is sound, because the meaning leads to it. ﴿Say: "Mock, [if you will]"﴾ is a command of threat. ﴿Indeed, Allah will bring out what you fear﴾, i.e., will make manifest what you were fearing, namely, you fear its disclosure from your hypocrisy. They used to fear that Allah would expose them through revelation concerning them, and through their mockery of Islam and its people. To the point that some of them said: "I would wish that I were brought forward and flogged a hundred times, and that nothing would be revealed about us that exposes us."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 9, verse 65:

﴿And if you ask them, they will surely say, "We were only conversing and playing."﴾ "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was marching in the expedition (*ghazwa*, military campaign) to Tabuk, and a group of the hypocrites were riding ahead of him, they said: 'Look at this man, who wants to conquer the palaces and fortresses of Syria! Far-fetched, far-fetched!' Then Allah informed His Prophet of this. So he (ﷺ) said, 'Hold back the riding party for me,' and he came to them and said, 'You said such-and-such.' They said, 'O Prophet of Allah, no, by Allah, we were not engaged in anything concerning your affair or the affair of your Companions, but we were engaged in something of what a riding party converses about, to shorten the journey for one another.'" That is, ﴿And if you ask them﴾ and you say to them, "Why did you say that?" they would say, ﴿We were only conversing and playing.﴾ ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad,

﴿Was it Allah and His signs and His Messenger that you were mocking?﴾ He did not give weight to their excuse, because they were lying in it. So they were treated as though they were admitting their mockery and that it existed in them, until they were rebuked for their error in placing the object of mockery in the position it occupies, since he placed the one mocked after the interrogative particle of affirmation (*taqrir*, a question that elicits confirmation). Here the particle is the hamza (ء) in the phrase ﴿أبِاللهِ﴾ ("Was it Allah…?"), and this is only sound after the mockery has been established.

Translation:

﴿Do not make excuses﴾: do not occupy yourselves with your false excuses, for they will not benefit you after your secret has been revealed. ﴿You have disbelieved﴾: you have made your disbelief manifest by your mockery. ﴿After your belief﴾: after you had displayed belief. ﴿If We pardon a group of you﴾: because of their repentance and their sincere belief after hypocrisy, ﴿We will punish another group because they were criminals﴾: persisting in hypocrisy and not repenting from it. (If "yu'fa" [a group is pardoned]) and ("tu'adhdhab ta'ifatun" [a group is punished]) are the readings of ʿĀṣim's transmission being excluded... 

Note: The final sentence, "غَيْرُ عاصِمٍ", is a reading-related remark stating that the variant in question is not the one transmitted by ʿĀṣim. It is translated here as: "(yu'fa) and (tu'adhdhab ta'ifatun) — not the reading of ʿĀṣim."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 9, verse 67:

(p-692) ﴿The hypocrite men and the hypocrite women are of one another.﴾ The hypocrite men were three hundred, and the hypocrite women were one hundred and seventy. ﴿They are of one another﴾ means: they are as if they were one soul. In this there is a denial that they are among the believers, and a refutation of their claim in His words: ﴿And they swear by God that they are truly of you﴾, and a confirmation of His words: ﴿And they are not of you﴾. He described them with what indicates the opposition of their state to the state of the believers, so He said: ﴿They enjoin what is evil﴾, meaning disbelief and disobedience.

﴿And they forbid what is good﴾, meaning obedience and faith. ﴿And they withhold their hands﴾, meaning they are stingy with giving, with charity, and with spending in the way of God.

﴿They have forgotten God﴾, meaning they abandoned His command, or neglected His remembrance. ﴿So He has forgotten them﴾, meaning He has left them without His mercy and His bounty.

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ They are the perfect ones in *fisq* (defiant disobedience), which is persistent rebellion in disbelief and complete departure from every good. And it is enough of a deterrent for the Muslim that he should fall into what earns him this foul name, the name with which the hypocrites were described when He went to the utmost in condemning them.

God has promised the hypocrites, men and women, and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, abiding therein (﴿خالِدِينَ فِيها﴾), intending to remain eternally in it. ﴿It is sufficient for them﴾ (﴿هِيَ حَسْبُهُمْ﴾), i.e., the Fire is sufficient for them. In this is an indication of the enormity of its punishment, and that it is of such a degree that nothing can be added to it. ﴿And God has cursed them﴾ (﴿وَلَعَنَهُمُ اللهُ﴾), and humiliated them along with the punishment, made them blameworthy, and joined them with the accursed devils.

﴿And for them is a lasting punishment﴾ (﴿وَلَهم عَذابٌ مُقِيمٌ﴾), constant and continuing with them in the present life, from which they never part. This is what they suffer of the weariness of hypocrisy, and of an outward appearance that contradicts their inner state out of fear of the Muslims, and of their constant dread of exposure and of the descent of punishment if their secrets were discovered.

The particle "al-kaf" in ﴿kaalladhīna min qablikum kānū ashadda minkum quwwatan wa-akthara amwālan wa-awlādan fa-istamtaʿū bi-khalāqihim fa-istamtaʿtum bi-khalāqikum kamā istamtaʿa alladhīna min qablikum bi-khalāqihim﴾ has a place in i'rab of raf' (nominative), meaning: "you are like those who came before you." Or it has a place of nasb (accusative), on the meaning: "you did the like of the deed of those who came before you," which is that you enjoyed your portion (khalāq) just as they enjoyed their portion, i.e., they took pleasure in the pleasures of this world. Al-khalāq (portion) is a derivative of al-khalq (creation/measurement), meaning what is created/decreed for the human being, in the sense of what has been decreed of good.

﴿wa-khuḍtum﴾ in falsehood ﴿ka-alladhī khāḍū﴾: like the company (fawj) who engaged, or like the immersion (khawḍ) in which they engaged. Al-khawḍ is entering into falsehood and frivolity. He mentioned ﴿fa-istamtaʿū bi-khalāqihim﴾ first, and His saying ﴿kamā istamtaʿa alladhīna min qablikum bi-khalāqihim﴾ is sufficient in place of it, in order to censure the former people for enjoying what they were given of the worldly portions and for being distracted by their perishable desires from considering the outcome and seeking success in the Hereafter. Then He likens the state of those addressed to their state. ﴿Fa-ulāʾika ḥabiṭat aʿmāluhum fī al-dunyā wa-al-ākhira﴾ in contrast to His saying: ﴿wa-ātaynāhu ajrahu fī al-dunyā wa-innahu fī al-ākhirati la-mina al-ṣāliḥīn﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 27]. ﴿Wa-ulāʾika humu al-khāsirūn﴾. Then He mentioned the report of those before them, saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 70:

﴿Has there not come to them the news of those before them: the people of Noah﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "those who" (alladhina). ﴿and ʿAd, Thamud, the people of Abraham, the companions of Madyan﴾, and the people of Madyan are the people of Shuʿayb. ﴿And the overturned cities (al-Mu'tafikat)﴾ are the cities of the people of Lot. Its i'tifak (overturning) means the reversal of their conditions from good to evil. ﴿Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, so Allah would not have wronged them﴾, meaning it was not proper for Him to wrong them by destroying them, because He is Wise, and so He does not punish them without a crime.

﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾ by disbelief and by denying the messengers.

The believing men and the believing women are allies of one another: in mutual support and mercy.

﴿They enjoin what is right﴾ by obedience and faith, ﴿and forbid what is wrong﴾ from associating partners with God and from disobedience. ﴿They establish prayer, give zakat, and obey God and His Messenger. Those—God will surely show them mercy﴾. The sin (sa-, "surely") here signifies that the mercy will certainly occur; it emphasizes the promise just as it emphasizes the threat in His saying: "I will surely take vengeance upon you someday." ﴿Indeed, God is Almighty﴾, Victorious over everything, Able over it; so He is able to grant reward and punishment. ﴿All-Wise﴾, placing each thing in its proper place.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on Surah 9, verse 72:

﴿Allah has promised the believing men and the believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and goodly dwellings.﴾ (Goodly dwellings) where life is pleasant. It is related from al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, that they are palaces of pearls, red rubies, and emeralds.

﴿In Gardens of Eden.﴾ *ʿAdn* is a proper noun (*ʿalam*), as shown by His saying: ﴿Gardens of Eden, which the Most Merciful promised to His servants﴾ [Maryam: 61]. You already know that *alladhi* and *allati* were placed to describe definite nouns by means of clauses (*al-jumal*). It is a city in Paradise.

﴿And approval from Allah﴾, meaning a portion of Allah's approval, ﴿is greater﴾ than all of that, because His approval is the cause of every success and happiness.

﴿That﴾ refers either to what He promised or to the approval, ﴿is the great triumph﴾, meaning the triumph alone, not what people regard as triumph.

O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers ﴿with the sword﴾ and the hypocrites ﴿with argument﴾, and be harsh toward them ﴿in both kinds of striving together, and do not show them leniency. Whoever is found to hold corruption in belief, this ruling applies to him: he is to be struggled against with argument, and harshness is to be employed with him to the extent possible﴾. ﴿And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾ — Hell.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 74:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained at Tabuk for two months, during which the Qur'an was being revealed to him, censuring the hypocrites who had stayed behind. Those among them who were with him would hear this. Among them was al-Jullas ibn Suwayd, who said: "By Allah, if what Muhammad says is true, concerning our brothers whom we left behind, who are our masters, then we are worse than donkeys." 'Amir ibn Qays al-Ansari said to al-Jullas: "Indeed, by Allah, Muhammad is truthful, and you are worse than a donkey." This reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he summoned them. He (al-Jullas) swore by Allah that he had not said it. 'Amir raised his hands and said: "O Allah, send down upon Your servant and Your Prophet the confirmation of the truthful one and the refutation of the liar." Then it was revealed: ﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say it, but they did indeed say the word of disbelief﴾, meaning: "If what Muhammad says is true, then we are worse than donkeys," or it was their mockery. Al-Jullas then said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I did say it, and 'Amir has spoken the truth." So al-Jullas repented, and his repentance was good.

﴿And they disbelieved after their Islam﴾, meaning they displayed their disbelief after they had displayed Islam. This indicates that faith (iman) and Islam are one, since He said: ﴿And they disbelieved after their Islam﴾.

﴿And they resolved upon what they did not attain﴾, namely the killing of Muhammad ﷺ, or the killing of 'Amir for his response to al-Jullas. It was also said: they intended to crown Ibn Ubayy, even though the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not pleased.

﴿And they found fault only in that Allah and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty﴾, meaning they disliked, denied, and criticized. This is because when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, they were in hardship of life, not riding horses, and not acquiring spoils. Then they were enriched by the booty. A client of al-Jullas was killed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered his blood-money to be twelve thousand, and so he became wealthy.

﴿So if they repent﴾ from hypocrisy, ﴿it will be better for them﴾, meaning the reward, and this is the verse at which al-Jullas repented. ﴿But if they turn away﴾, persisting in hypocrisy, ﴿Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter﴾, by killing and by the Fire. ﴿And they will have no protector or helper on earth﴾ who could save them from the punishment.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 75:

﴿Among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾. It is related that Tha'labah ibn Hatib said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He grants me wealth." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Tha'labah, a little that you can give thanks for is better than a lot that you cannot bear." He returned to him and said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, if He grants me wealth, I will surely give to everyone who has a right his right." So he (ﷺ) prayed for him, and he acquired sheep, which multiplied as worms multiply, until the city could no longer hold them. He moved to a valley and cut himself off from the Friday prayer and the congregation. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked about him, and it was said: "His wealth has grown so much that a valley can no longer contain it." He said: "Woe to Tha'labah!" (p-696) The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then sent collectors (musaddiqin) to take the sadaqat (obligatory charity). The people met them with their sadaqat, and the two passed by Tha'labah and asked him for the sadaqah. He said: "This is nothing but jizyah (poll tax)," and said: "Go back until I consider my opinion." When they returned, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them before they spoke to him: "Woe to Tha'labah!" twice. Then this verse was revealed. Tha'labah came with the sadaqah and said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden me to accept it from you." So he put dust on his head. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away, and he brought it to Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), who did not accept it, and he brought it to Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) during his caliphate, who did not accept it either. He died in the time of Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him).

﴿If He gives us of His bounty﴾, i.e., wealth, ﴿we will surely give charity﴾, i.e., we will surely pay the sadaqah. The original form is "latatasaddaqanna," but the taa' was assimilated into the saad (idgham, merging of one letter into another) because they are close in articulation: ﴿and we will surely be among the righteous﴾ by paying the sadaqah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 76:

﴿When He gave them of His bounty﴾ Allah gave them wealth, and they attained their wishes. ﴿they became miserly with it﴾ they withheld the right of Allah, and did not fulfil the covenant.

﴿and turned away﴾ from obedience to Allah, ﴿while they were averse﴾ persisting in aversion.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 77:

﴿So He caused them to follow up hypocrisy in their hearts﴾: He caused the stinginess to leave them with hypocrisy firmly settled in their hearts, because it was the cause of it. ﴿Until the Day they meet Him﴾: that is, the recompense of their deed, which is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Because they failed Allah in what they promised Him and because they used to lie﴾: due to their failing to fulfil what they had promised Allah, namely giving charity and righteousness, and due to their being liars. And from this: failing to keep a promise has been made one third of hypocrisy.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 78:

﴿Did they not know﴾ meaning: the hypocrites, ﴿that Allah knows their secret﴾ what they concealed of hypocrisy, by resolving to break what they had promised Him, ﴿and their private counsel﴾ and what they confided to one another among themselves of slander against the religion, calling the charity (ṣadaqah) a jizyah (poll-tax), and planning to withhold it.

﴿And that Allah is the Knower of the unseen⁠—﴾ so nothing is hidden from Him.

**﴿Alladhina﴾** (the relative pronoun *alladhina*) may be in the accusative case, or in the nominative by way of *dhamm* (censure, a shift to blame), or in the genitive as a *badal* (substitute, apposition) for the pronoun in ﴿their secret and their private talk﴾. ﴿Yalmizuna al-mutawwi'in﴾ means they find fault with (*yaʿību*) the *mutawwiʿin*, the volunteers, those who give voluntarily. ﴿Min al-mu'minin fi al-sadaqat﴾: the phrase ﴿min al-mu'minin﴾ is related to *yalmizuna*. It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) urged people to give charity, and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf came with four thousand dirhams and said, "I had eight thousand. I lent four to my Lord and kept four for my dependants." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "May Allah bless you in what you gave and in what you kept." So Allah blessed him, until his wife Tumadir was reconciled to a quarter of the eighth (of his estate) for eighty thousand. ʿAsim gave a hundred *wasq* of dates (a *wasq* being a measure of sixty *sa'*).

﴿Wa alladhina﴾ is coordinated (*ʿatf*) with ﴿al-mutawwiʿin﴾. ﴿La yajidun illa juhdahum﴾ means their capacity (*taqatahum*). It is narrated from Nafiʿ that he read *jahdahum*, and the two (*juhd* and *jahd*) are the same in meaning. It is also said that *al-juhd* means capacity and *al-jahd* means hardship. Abu ʿAqil came with one *sa'* of dates and said, "I spent my night drawing water with a rope for two *sa'*, so I left one *sa'* for my dependants and brought one *sa'*." The hypocrites found fault with them and said, "ʿAbd al-Rahman and ʿAsim gave only out of show (*riya'*), and as for the *sa'* of Abu ʿAqil, Allah has no need of it." ﴿Fa yaskharuna minhum﴾ means so they mock them (*fa yahzaʾuna*). ﴿Sakhira Allah minhum﴾: Allah requited them for their mockery. This is a statement of information, not a supplication. ﴿Wa lahum ʿadhabun alim﴾ means a painful (*muʾlim*) punishment.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 80:

When ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to seek forgiveness for his father during his illness, the verse was revealed: ﴿Seek forgiveness for them, or do not seek forgiveness for them﴾. It has already been mentioned that this command is in the sense of a statement (khabar), as if it were said: "Allah will not forgive them whether you seek forgiveness for them or do not seek forgiveness for them." ﴿If you seek forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will still not forgive them﴾. The seventy is used, in their speech, like a proverb (mathal) for multiplicity (li-l-takthir), and it is not meant as a specific limit or ultimate end. For if he sought forgiveness for them for the duration of his life, Allah would not forgive them, because they are disbelievers, and Allah does not forgive one who disbelieves in Him. The meaning is: even if you exceed in seeking forgiveness, Allah will not forgive them. Reports have come mentioning the seventy, and all of them indicate multiplicity, not a specific limit or end. As for the reason for singling out seventy from among the other numbers: numbers are either few or many; the few is what is below three, and the many is three and above; the least of the many is three, and its upper extent has no end. Numbers are also of two kinds: even (shaf') and odd (watr); the first of the even numbers is two, and the first of the odd numbers is three, while one is not a number. Seven is the first collective number of many that combines both kinds, for in it there are three odd numbers and three even numbers. Ten is the completion of counting, for whatever exceeds ten is the addition of units to ten, as in your saying: twelve, thirteen, up to twenty; twenty is the repetition of ten twice, thirty is its repetition three times, and so on up to a hundred. Seventy thus combines multiplicity, the kind (nawʿ), and the multiplicity of that kind, and the completion of counting and the multiplicity within it. Thus seventy becomes the least of the many numbers in every respect, and it has no ultimate end. So it is possible that seventy was singled out for this meaning, and Allah knows best. ﴿That﴾ refers to despair of forgiveness, ﴿because they﴾ — because they ﴿disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger﴾ — and there is no forgiveness for the disbelievers. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾, those who have gone outside faith, as long as they choose disbelief and transgression.

﴿Those who were left behind rejoiced﴾ the hypocrites who asked permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he granted them leave and left them behind in Madinah during the expedition of Tabuk; or those whom their laziness, their hypocrisy, and Satan left behind.

﴿in their sitting﴾ in their remaining behind from the expedition. ﴿in opposition to the Messenger of Allah﴾ opposing him. It is a maf'ul lahu (object of purpose) or a hal (circumstantial accusative), meaning: they sat behind in order to oppose him, or as those opposing him.

﴿and they disliked striving with their wealth and their selves in the way of Allah﴾ i.e., they did not do what the believers did of spending their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah. And how could they not dislike it, when they did not have what the believers have of the impulse of faith and the call of certainty?

﴿And they said: Do not go forth in the heat﴾ some of them said to others, or they said to the believers, discouraging them. ﴿Say: The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood﴾ a rebuke of their ignorance, because whoever guards himself from the hardship of an hour, and as a result of that guarding falls into the hardship of eternity, is more ignorant than every ignorant person.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 82:

﴿So let them laugh a little and let them weep much﴾ That is: they will laugh a little, out of their joy at staying behind in this world, and they will weep much as a recompense in the Hereafter. However, it has been expressed in the form of a command, to indicate that this is a binding decree that cannot be otherwise. It is related that the people of hypocrisy will weep in the Fire throughout the lifespan of this world, their tears never drying up, and they will not know the comfort of sleep,

﴿as a recompense for what they used to earn﴾ of hypocrisy.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 83:

﴿So if Allah returns you﴾: that is, brings you back from Tabuk. He said ﴿to a group of them﴾ because some of them had repented of hypocrisy, and some of them had perished.

﴿Then they ask your permission to go out﴾ to a military expedition (ghazwah) after the expedition of Tabuk. ﴿So say: "You will never go out with me, ever."﴾ With the ya' pronounced with sukun (silent): Hamzah, ʿAli, and Abu Bakr.

﴿And you will never fight with me against an enemy.﴾ The word (maʿiya) with the ya' vowelled: Hafs.

﴿Indeed, you were content to sit back the first time﴾: at the first time you were called to the expedition of Tabuk. ﴿So sit back with﴾ ﴿those who stayed behind﴾: with those who remained behind after that.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 84:

The son of ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, who was a believer, asked the Prophet ﷺ to shroud his father in his shirt and to pray over him, and he agreed. ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) objected to this, so the Prophet ﷺ said: "That will not benefit him, but I hope that a thousand of his people will become Muslim through it." Then the verse was revealed: ﴿And do not pray over any of them who has died, ever, from among the hypocrites﴾, meaning the funeral prayer (ṣalāt al-janāzah). It is narrated that a thousand men of the Khazraj embraced Islam when they saw him (p-700) seeking blessing through the garment of the Prophet ﷺ.

﴿Died﴾ is a description of ﴿anyone﴾, and ﴿ever﴾ is an adverbial of time for ﴿pray﴾ (tuṣalli). When the Prophet ﷺ had buried a deceased person, he would stand at his grave and supplicate for him. So it was said: ﴿And do not stand at his grave. Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and they died while defiantly disobedient﴾. This is a reason given for the prohibition, meaning: they are not deserving of prayer over them, because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger.

This is a passage from al-Nasafi's Madarik al-Tanzil, and it contains a Qur'anic verse. Translation:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 85:

﴿And let not their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through them in this world, and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers.﴾ The repetition (al-takrir) is for emphasis (al-mubalaghah) and confirmation (al-ta'kid), and so that it remains in the mind of the addressee, who does not forget it and believes it to be important; and because every verse is [addressed] to a group other than the other group.

﷿ "And when a surah is sent down" — it is permissible that by "a surah" is meant a complete surah, and it is permissible that by it is meant part of a surah, just as "the Qur'an" and "the Book" are applied to the whole and to a part of it. ﴿That believe in Allah⦆ — meaning, "that they believe," or the "an" here is the explanatory (al-mufassira, the "an" that explains what precedes it). ﴿And strive with His Messenger⦆ — "Those of wealth among them ask your permission, and say, 'Leave us, that we may be with those who sit (at home).'" Ulu al-tawl (ulu al-tawl) means those possessed of bounty and ample means. ﴿With those who sit (at home)⦆ means with those who have an excuse for staying behind, such as the sick and the chronically disabled (al-zamna).

Note: The Qur'anic quotations above are rendered in translation; the bracketed phrases are the translator's rendering of the Qur'anic text as it appears in the source.

﷽

﴿They were content to be with the women who remain behind (al-khawalif)﴾, i.e., the women; al-khawalif is the plural of khalifah. ﴿And a seal was set upon their hearts﴾, i.e., it was sealed over them, because of their choosing disbelief and hypocrisy. ﴿So they do not understand﴾ what there is in jihad of success and felicity, and what there is in staying behind of destruction and wretchedness.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 88:

﴿But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their selves.﴾ (p-701) That is: if these (hypocrites) stay behind, then those who are better than them have risen up to the raid. ﴿And those, they are the successful﴾, the ones who attain every desired goal.
Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph. His saying "has prepared" (a'adda) is evidence that they (the gardens) are created.

The commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 90:

﴿And those who make excuses among the Bedouins came, seeking permission to be excused﴾. Al-mu'adhdhirun is one who is excused in a matter when he falls short in it and is negligent. Its real meaning is that he gives the impression that he has an excuse for what he did, while he has no excuse. Alternatively, it is read al-mu'tadhirun (المُعْتَذِرُونَ), with the ta' assimilated into the dhal and its vowel transferred to the 'ayn, and they are those who make excuses falsely. It is said: they were Asad and Ghatafan, who said: "Indeed we have dependents, and indeed we are in hardship, so permit us to stay behind." ﴿And those who lied to Allah and His Messenger sat back﴾. They are the hypocrites among the Bedouins who neither came nor made excuses, so it became clear by this that they had lied to Allah and His Messenger in their claim of faith. ﴿There will afflict those among them who disbelieved﴾, from among the Bedouins, ﴿a painful punishment﴾: in this world by killing, and in the Hereafter by the Fire.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 91:

﴿There is no blame upon the weak﴾ the aged and the chronically ill, ﴿nor upon the sick﴾ nor upon ﴿those who find nothing to spend﴾ — they are the poor among Muzayna, Juhayna and Banu ʿUdhra. ﴿Blame﴾ (ḥaraj) means sin and constraint in lagging behind. ﴿When they are sincere toward Allah and His Messenger﴾ by believing openly and secretly, and obeying, as the sincere advisor (nasih) acts toward his companion. ﴿There is no path against the good-doers﴾ — the excused ones who give sincere counsel — ﴿against them﴾ meaning: there is no fault upon them, and no way to reproach them. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾ — He forgives their staying behind — ﴿Merciful﴾ toward them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 92:

﴿Nor [is there blame] upon those who came to you that you might provide them with mounts,﴾ i.e., that you might give them mounts (al-ḥumūlah). ﴿[And] you said,﴾ qulta is a ḥāl (circumstantial clause) relating to the kāf in atawka, and qad is implied before it; i.e., when they came to you saying, ﴿"I cannot find anything to mount you upon,"﴾ tawallaw is the response (jawāb) of idhā. ﴿And their eyes overflowed with tears,﴾ i.e., flowed, as in your saying: tafīḍu damʿan (they overflow with tears). This is more eloquent than tafīḍu damʿuhā (its tears overflow), because the eye is treated as though all of it were overflowing tears. The min here is for explanation (lil-bayān), as in your saying: afdīka min rajul (I would ransom you from a man). The place of the prepositional phrase is accusative as a specification (tamyīz). It is also permissible that qulta lā ajidu be a resumptive clause (isti'nāf), as if it were said: "When they came to you that you might mount them, they turned away," and it was said: "What is the matter with them that they turned away weeping?" and it was said: ﴿"You said, 'I cannot find anything to mount you upon.'"﴾ except that it is placed in the middle between the condition and the response, like a parenthetical insertion. ﴿Grief﴾ is an object of purpose (maf'ūl lahu). ﴿That they might not find what they could spend.﴾ That is, lest they should not find what they could spend. Its place is accusative as an object of purpose, and the governing word is ḥazanan (grief). Those who sought mounts were Abū Mūsā al-Ash'arī and his companions, or the weepers, and they were six men from the Anṣār.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 93:

﴿The blame lies only on those who ask you for permission﴾ to stay behind [in the campaign] ﴿while they are rich﴾. His saying ﴿They are content﴾ is a resumptive sentence (isti'naf), as if it were said: "What is their state that they asked for permission while they are rich?!" So it was said: "They are content."

﴿To be with those left behind (al-khawalif)﴾, i.e., by being included in the group of those left behind (al-khawalif). ﴿And Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not know.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 94:

﴿They make excuses to you﴾: they fabricate for themselves a false excuse. ﴿When you return to them﴾: from this journey. ﴿Say: Do not make excuses﴾ with falsehood. ﴿We will never believe you﴾: we will never accept you as truthful. This is the reason for the prohibition against making excuses, because the aim of one who makes an excuse is to be believed regarding what he offers as an excuse. ﴿Allah has already informed us of your news﴾: this is the reason for the negation of their being believed, because when Allah, exalted is He, revealed to His Messenger the information about their news and what is in their inner selves, it would not be consistent, along with that, to believe them in their excuses. ﴿And Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger﴾: will you repent or will you remain steadfast upon your disbelief? ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾: that is, you will be returned to Him, and He is the Knower of (p-703) every secret and every open matter. ﴿So He will inform you of what you used to do﴾: so He will recompense you according to that.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 95:

﴿They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them, that you may leave them alone.﴾ That is, that you would abandon them and not rebuke them. ﴿So leave them alone.﴾ That is, give them what they seek. ﴿Indeed, they are defilement.﴾ This is a reason (ta'līl) for abandoning reproach of them; that is, reproach does not benefit them and does not reform them, because they are filth (arjās), and there is no way to purify them. ﴿And their refuge is Hell.﴾ Their destination is the Fire; meaning, the Fire suffices them as reproach and rebuke, so do not burden yourselves with reproaching them. ﴿As recompense for what they used to earn.﴾ That is, they are repaid the recompense of their earning.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 96:

﴿They swear to you that you may be pleased with them.﴾ That is: their aim in swearing by Allah is to seek your pleasure, so that this may benefit them in their worldly affairs. ﴿But if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with the defiant people.﴾ That is: your pleasure alone does not benefit them when Allah is displeased with them, and they are exposed to the immediate and the delayed of His punishment. This was said only so that it would not be imagined that the pleasure of the believers entails the pleasure of Allah with them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 97:

﴿The Bedouins﴾ (al-A'rab), the people of the desert, are ﴿more intense in disbelief and hypocrisy﴾ than the people of the settled towns (al-hadar), because of their harshness (jafa'), their hardness of heart (qaswa), and their remoteness from knowledge (ilm) and the scholars (ulama).

﴿And more likely not to know﴾ (wa-ajdaru alla ya'lamu), meaning: more deserving of not knowing ﴿the limits of what Allah has sent down to His Messenger﴾. That is: the limits of the religion and the laws and rulings that Allah has sent down. Among this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed harshness and hardness are among the fadaddin," meaning the ukra (plowmen/farmhands), because they fadd, that is, they shout at their plowing animals. Al-fadid is shouting.

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of their conditions,

﴿All-Wise﴾ in granting them respite.

(p-704)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 98:

﴿And among the Bedouins is one who takes what he spends﴾ i.e., gives in charity, ﴿as a loss﴾, a penalty and a ruin, because he spends only out of fear (taqiyya) of the Muslims and for show (riya'), not for the sake of Allah's Face and seeking reward from Him.

﴿And he waits for misfortunes to befall you﴾ i.e., the turns (dawa'ir) of time and the changing of conditions through the revolution of days, so that your ascendancy over him may pass and he may be freed from giving charity.

﴿The evil turn is upon them﴾ i.e., upon them revolve the calamities and wars which they expect to befall the Muslims. (Al-Su'): Makki and Abu 'Amr read it with a damma, and it means punishment. And (al-Saw'), with a fatha, is a dispraise of the turn, as in your saying "a man of evil" (rajul saw'), in contrast to your saying "a man of truth" (rajul sidq).

﴿And Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of what they say when charity is imposed upon them, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of what they conceal.

(p-705)

﴿And among the Bedouin are those who believe in God and the Last Day, and take what they spend﴾ in the way of jihad and charitable gifts

﴿as means of nearness﴾: means of drawing near (qurbah) ﴿to God﴾. This is the second object of ﴿yattakhidhu﴾ (takes). ﴿And the prayers of the Messenger﴾, meaning his supplication, because he, peace be upon him, used to pray for good and blessing upon those who gave charity and would ask forgiveness for them, as in his saying: "O God, bless the family of Abi Awfa." ﴿Indeed, it﴾, that is, the expenditure, or the prayers of the Messenger, ﴿is a means of nearness for them﴾. (Qurbatun) is read by Nafi'. This is a testimony from God to the giver in confirmation of what he believed, that his spending constitutes means of nearness and prayers, and a confirmation of his hope. It comes in the form of an resumption (istinaf, a new independent sentence), together with the two particles of alerting (tanbih) and affirmation (tahqiq), which indicate the firmness and certainty of the matter. Likewise, ﴿God will admit them into His mercy﴾, that is, His Garden. The sin (sawf) in the verb indicates the certainty of the promise. How strongly this statement indicates God's pleasure with the charitable givers, and that charity from Him holds a place when the intention of its giver is sincere! ﴿Indeed, God is Forgiving﴾, who conceals the fault of the one who falls short, ﴿Merciful﴾, who accepts the effort of the one of limited means.

The Foremost and First (al-sabiqun al-awwalun)

﴿And the foremost ones﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), ﴿the first﴾ is a qualifier (sifah) for them, ﴿from among the Emigrants (al-muhajirin)﴾ is a specification (tabyin) for them. They are those who prayed towards both qiblas, or those who witnessed Badr, or the Pledge of al-Ridwan (bay'at al-Ridwan).

﴿And the Helpers (al-ansar)﴾ is conjoined (ʿatf) to "the Emigrants," meaning: and from among the Helpers. They are the people of the First Pledge of al-ʿAqabah, who were seven men, and the people of the Second Pledge of al-ʿAqabah, who were seventy. ﴿And those who followed them in excellence (bi-ihsan)﴾ from among the Emigrants and the Helpers, so they were the rest of the Companions. It has also been said: they are those who followed them in faith and obedience until the Day of Resurrection. The predicate (khabar) is: ﴿Allah is pleased with them﴾ for their good deeds, ﴿and they are pleased with Him﴾ for what He has bestowed upon them of His religious and worldly blessings. ﴿And He has prepared for them﴾ is conjoined to "is pleased," ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ (min tahtiha) is read by Makki,

﴿abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 101:

﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites﴾, meaning: around your town, which is Medina. ﴿And among the people of Medina﴾ [are hypocrites]. They are Juhayna, Aslam, Ashja', and Ghifar, who were dwelling around it.

﴿And among the people of Medina﴾ is a conjunction with the predicate of the subject, which is "among those around you." The subject is ﴿hypocrites﴾. It is permissible for it to be a sentence conjoined to the subject and predicate, if you estimate: ﴿And among the people of Medina﴾ [there are] people ﴿who have become accustomed to hypocrisy﴾, meaning: they have become adept at it, with ﴿who have become accustomed﴾ being a descriptive attribute of an omitted noun. On the first interpretation, it is either a new independent statement, or a descriptive attribute of "hypocrites," separated from it by a conjunction with its predicate. He indicated their skill in it by His saying: ﴿You do not know them﴾, meaning: they are concealed from you despite your shrewdness and the soundness of your insight, due to their extreme care in avoiding anything that would cast doubt on their affair. Then He said: ﴿We know them﴾, meaning: none knows them except Allah, and none other than Him is informed of their secret, because they conceal disbelief in the blackness of their hearts while showing you outwardly the appearance of sincere believers. ﴿We will punish them twice﴾ (p-706). They are: killing and the punishment of the grave; or disgrace and the punishment of the grave; or the taking of charities from their wealth and the wearing down of their bodies.

﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾, meaning: the punishment of the Fire.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on Surah 9, verse 102:**

﴿And others﴾, that is, other people besides those mentioned, ﴿who have acknowledged their sins﴾. That is, they did not offer false excuses for their staying behind as others did, but they acknowledged against themselves that they had done a wretched thing, and they were full of regret. They were ten in number. "Seven of them, when news of what had been revealed about those who stayed behind reached them, tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived, entered the mosque, and prayed two rak'ahs (his custom whenever he returned from a journey). He saw them tied up and asked about them. They told him that they had sworn not to untie themselves until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself untied them. He said: 'And I swear that I will not untie them until I am commanded concerning them.' Then (the revelation) came down, and he released them. They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this is our wealth which kept us away from you, so accept it as charity and purify us.' He said: 'I was not commanded to take anything of your wealth.' Then there came down: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾."

﴿They mixed a righteous deed﴾, namely going out to the jihad, ﴿with another evil﴾, namely staying behind from it, or (the evil is) repentance and sin. This is from their saying: "I sold the sheep for a sheep and a dirham," meaning: a sheep for a dirham. Thus the particle waw (وَ) is used in the sense of the particle ba' (بِ), because waw indicates joining together (لِلْجَمْعِ) and ba' indicates attachment (لِلْإلْصاقِ), so the two are compatible.

Alternatively, the meaning is: the mixing of each of the two with the other, so each of them is mixed and is that with which something is mixed. This is like your saying: "I mixed the water and the milk," meaning: "I mixed each of them with its counterpart." This differs from your saying: "I mixed the water with the milk," because in that case you made the water the thing mixed and the milk the thing it was mixed with. But when you say it with waw, you have made the water and the milk both mixed and the thing mixed with both of them, as if you had said: "I mixed the water with the milk, and the milk with the water."

﴿It may be that Allah will turn to them in forgiveness; indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾. He did not mention their repentance, because He mentioned their acknowledgment of their sins, and this is an indication of repentance.

﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾ as an expiation for their sins. It was said: it is the zakat (obligatory almsgiving). ﴿That purifies them﴾ from sins. It is a description of ṣadaqah, and the tā' (in tuṭahhiruhum) is for address (the second person), or for the absent feminine (ghaybat al-mu'annath). The tā' in ﴿and purifies them﴾ (watuzakkīhim) is necessarily for address. ﴿Through it﴾, through the charity, and tazkiyah (purification) is an intensification of tathhīr (purification) and an increase in it, or it means growth and blessing in the wealth. ﴿And pray for them﴾, and show kindness to them by supplicating for them and asking for mercy on their behalf. The sunna (the prophetic practice) is that the one collecting the charity supplicates for the owner of the charity when he takes it. ﴿Indeed, your prayer﴾ (ṣalawātika), with the reading of the Kufans other than Abu Bakr, it was said: ṣalāh (prayer, in the singular) is more comprehensive than ṣalawāt (prayers, in the plural), because it refers to the category.

﴿A source of tranquility for them﴾, they find rest in it, and their hearts are reassured that Allah has accepted their repentance. ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of your supplication, or All-Hearing of their acknowledgment of their sins and their supplication. ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of what is in their hearts of regret and grief over what they had neglected.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 104:

﴿Did they not know﴾ The intended meaning is: those upon whom repentance is accepted. That is, did they not know before repentance was accepted from them and their charities (ṣadaqāt) were accepted?

﴿That it is God who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ when it is sound, ﴿and takes the charities﴾ and accepts them when they come from sincerity of intention. The word هو (huwa, "He") here is for restriction (al-takhṣīṣ, specification), meaning: this is not up to the Messenger of God (ﷺ); rather, God is the One who accepts repentance and rejects it. So aim at Him with it, and direct it to Him.

﴿And that God is the One who is al-Tawwāb (the Oft-Returning, Accepting of Repentance)﴾, abundant in accepting repentance, ﴿al-Raḥīm (the Most Merciful)﴾, who pardons the sin (al-ḥawba).

﴿And say﴾ to these repentant ones: ﴿Work, and Allah will see your work, and His Messenger and the believers﴾. That is: your deeds are not hidden from Allah and His servants, whether good or bad, as you have seen and as has become clear to you. Or it is addressed to those who have not repented, as encouragement for them to repent. It is narrated that when they were forgiven, those who had not repented said: "These who repented were with us yesterday, not spoken to and not sat with. What is their situation?" So this verse was revealed. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿then Allah will see﴾, is a warning to them and a caution against the consequences of persistence and of neglecting repentance.

﴿And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ (p. 708), that which is hidden from people and that which they witness, ﴿and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, informing you as a reminder and recompensing you for it.

(And others are deferred until Allah's command) — read without the hamza by Madani and by Kufan readers other than Abu Bakr; the others read (mur'jawna) from arja'tuhu and arjatuhu, meaning "I delayed it," from which comes the word al-Murji'ah (those who defer judgment on actions). The meaning: and others among those who stayed behind are held in suspense until Allah's command regarding them becomes manifest. ﴿Either He will punish them﴾ if they persist and do not repent, ﴿or He will relent toward them﴾ if they repent. They were three: Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayyah, and Murarah ibn al-Rabi'. The key point is that they were from Medina, not Mecca, and they stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk; they are the ones mentioned in His saying: ﴿And [He also relented toward] the three who were left behind﴾. ﴿Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of their hope, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in deferring them. "Imma" (either/or) here expresses uncertainty, and this uncertainty relates to the servants: that is, fear punishment for them, and hope for mercy for them. It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded his companions not to greet them or speak to them. They did not do what that group did of tying themselves to the pillars and displaying grief and distress. When they realized that no one was looking at them, they entrusted their affair to Allah, sincerely purified their intentions, and their repentance was pure, so Allah had mercy on them.

**﴿And those who took a mosque﴾.** Its implied construction is: "and [among] them are those who took." The reading without the *waw* (conjunction) is that of the Madani (the reading of Medina) and the Shami (the reading of Syria). The phrase is a *mubtada'* (grammatical subject) whose *khabar* (predicate) is omitted; the sense is: "We recompensed them."

It is narrated that when the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf built the Mosque of Quba, they sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asking him to come to them. He came and prayed in it. Their brothers, the Banu Ghanm ibn 'Awf, envied them and said: "We will build a mosque and send to the Messenger of Allah to pray in it." Abu 'Amir the monk, who had come from Syria, would pray in it. He was the one who said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud: "I do not find a people who fight you except that I fight them along with them." He did not cease fighting him until the day of Hunayn. So they built a mosque beside the Mosque of Quba and said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "We have built a mosque for the one who is sick and in need, and we love that you pray in it for us." He said: "I am on the wing of a journey. When we return from Tabuk, if Allah wills, we will pray in it." When he returned from the expedition of Tabuk, they asked him to come to the mosque, and this verse was revealed to him. He said to Wahshi, the slayer of Hamza, and Ma'n ibn 'Adi and others: "Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, demolish it and burn it." They did so, and he ordered that its site be made a dunghill into which carrion and refuse were thrown. Abu 'Amir died in Syria.

﴿harm﴾ is an object of purpose (*maf'ul lahu*; the noun that states the reason for the action), and so is what follows it: ﴿harm to their brothers, the people of the Mosque of Quba﴾; ﴿and disbelief﴾, that is, strengthening hypocrisy; ﴿and division among the believers﴾, because they used to pray together in the Mosque of Quba, so they wanted to scatter them from it and cause their word to differ; ﴿and an ambush for whoever﴾, that is, preparing for the sake of ﴿whoever fought Allah and His Messenger﴾, and he is the monk. They prepared it for him so that he would pray in it and prevail over the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

It was said: every mosque built for boasting, or for show, or for reputation, or for a purpose other than seeking the face of Allah, or with money that is not lawful, is akin to the Mosque of Harm.

﴿from before﴾ is connected to "fought," meaning: from before the building of this mosque, that is, on the day of the Trench. ﴿And they will surely swear﴾ falsely ﴿that we intended only the good﴾: we did not intend, by building this mosque, anything but the best aspect, which is prayer, the remembrance of Allah, and the provision of space for those who pray. ﴿And Allah bears witness that they are indeed liars﴾ in their oath.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 108:

﴿Do not stand in it ever﴾ for prayer. ﴿A mosque founded upon piety⁠﴾ from the first day. The *lam* here is the *lam al-ibtida'* (the lam of beginning, emphasis). "Founded" (*ussisa*) is a *na't* (qualifier) of it. It is the Mosque of Quba', which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) founded, and he prayed in it during the days of his stay at Quba'. Or it is the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina. ﴿From the first day⁠﴾ means from the first of the days of its existence. It has been said: the *qiyas* (expected usage) in this is "*mudh*," because it denotes the endpoint in time, while "*min*" denotes the starting point of an extent in place. The answer is that "*min*" is general, applying to both time and place. ﴿Is worthier that you stand in it⁠﴾ as one praying. ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves⁠﴾. It has been said: "When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) walked, and with him were the Emigrants, until they stopped at the door of the Mosque of Quba'. There the Ansar were sitting, and he said: 'Are you believers?' The people were silent. He repeated it, and 'Umar said: 'O Messenger of Allah, they are indeed believers, and I am with them.' He (ﷺ) said: 'Are you content with the decree?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Will you be patient in affliction?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Will you give thanks in ease?' They said: 'Yes.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'You are believers, by the Lord of the Ka'bah.' Then he sat down and said: 'O assembly of the Ansar, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has praised you. What do you do at wudu' and after relieving yourselves?' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we follow the excrement with three stones, then we follow the stones with water.' Then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Men who love to purify themselves⁠﴾." It has been said: it is general in purifying oneself from all impurities. It has also been said: it is purification from sins through repentance. The meaning of their love for purification is that they prefer it and are eager for it, as the lover is eager for the beloved. The meaning of Allah's love for them is that He is pleased with them and bestows favor upon them, as a lover does with his beloved.

﴿Is one who has founded his building﴾ laid the foundation of what he builds ﴿upon piety from God and His good pleasure, better﴾ ﴿or one who has founded his building upon the edge of a crumbling precipice﴾ This is a rhetorical question (su'al taqrir), and its answer is left unstated because it is obvious. The meaning is: ﴿Is one who has founded﴾ the structure of his religion ﴿upon a firm base, namely the piety of God and His good pleasure, better, or one who has founded it upon a base that is the weakest of foundations (p-711), namely falsehood and hypocrisy, whose likeness is that of a crumbling precipice's edge in its lack of stability and firmness?" The edge of the precipice (shafa jurf) is placed in opposition to piety, because it is made a figure (majaz) for what contradicts piety. Shafa means the lip and the brink. The jurf of a valley is its side, whose base is hollowed out by water and which the torrents wash away, so that it remains weak. Al-har (هار) means the one that is crumbling, which has split and is on the verge of collapsing and falling. Its pattern is fa'l, which falls short of fa'il, like khalf from khalif. Its alif is not the alif of the active participle (fa'il); rather it is its middle radical, and its original form is hawr, which was changed to an alif because it was vowelled and the letter before it was open. You will find no expression more eloquent than this one, nor more indicative of the reality of falsehood and the essence of its matter.

(Afaman ussisa bunyanuhu) and (Amman ussisa bunyanuhu) are read by al-Shami and Nafi'. (Jurfin) is read by al-Shami, Hamza, and Yahya. (Har) with imala (the vowel-raising reading) is read by Abu 'Amr, Hamza in one transmission, and Yahya.

﴿So it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell﴾ Thus falsehood plunged him into the fire of Hell. Since he made the crumbling precipice a figure for falsehood, he maintained the figure (tarshih al-majaz), so he used the word for collapse, which belongs to the precipice, so that one would picture the one who follows falsehood as though he had founded his building upon the edge of a crumbling precipice over one of the valleys of Hell, and that precipice collapsed with him, so he fell to its bottom. Jabir said: "I saw smoke coming out of the Mosque of Harm when it collapsed." ﴿And God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ He does not grant them success toward good, as a punishment for them for their hypocrisy.

(p-٧١٢)

﴿Their building which they built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts.﴾ Its demolition will not cease to be a cause of doubt and of hypocrisy increasing beyond their existing doubt and hypocrisy, because of what angered them about it and weighed heavily upon them. ﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾ is the reading of al-Shami (the Syrian reader, Ibn ʿAmir), Hamza, and Hafs, meaning: ﴿unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾ in the sense of *tatagatta‘u* (تَتَقَطَّعُ). According to others, it is *tuqatta‘a* (تُقَطَّعَ), meaning: ﴿unless their hearts are cut into pieces﴾ and divided into parts, at which point they will forget about it. As for while their hearts remain whole and united, the doubt remains within them, firmly established. Then it is permissible that the mention of cutting is a depiction of the state of the doubt's removal from them. It is also permissible that the literal cutting of them is intended, and what will befall them of that by their being killed, or in the graves, or in the Fire. Or its meaning is: ﴿unless they repent with a repentance by which their hearts are cut to pieces﴾ through remorse and grief over their negligence. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of their resolves, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in the recompense for their crimes.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 111:

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth, in return for which they shall have Paradise﴾. Allah has likened His rewarding them with Paradise, in return for their giving up their lives and their wealth in His cause, to a purchase (bi-l-shira'). It is also narrated: He dealt with them in trade (tajarahum) and raised the price (fa-aghla) for them. From al-Hasan: the "lives" are those He created, and the "wealth" is that which He provided. A bedouin (a'rabi) passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was reciting it, and said: "By Allah, it is a profitable sale; we will not cancel it, nor will we ask for its cancellation." Then he went out to the raid and was martyred.

﴿They fight in the way of Allah﴾: an explanation of the place of surrender. ﴿So they kill and are killed﴾: that is, at times they kill the enemy, and at other times the enemy kills them. (Thus they are killed and they kill): Hamzah and Ali.

﴿A promise binding upon Him﴾: a verbal noun (masdar), meaning He promised them this as a promise, ﴿true﴾: this is its attribute. He informs that this promise which He made to those who strive in His cause is a firm promise, one which He has affirmed.

﴿In the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an﴾: this is evidence that the people of every religious community (millah) were commanded to fight and were promised reward for it. Then He said: ﴿And who is more faithful to his covenant than Allah?﴾ because breaking a promise is ugly, and no generous person among us would undertake it, so how much less the Most Generous of the generous! We see no more eloquent or better encouragement to jihad than this. ﴿So rejoice in your transaction which you have made﴾: rejoice with the utmost joy, for you are selling what is perishable for what is everlasting.

﴿And that is the great triumph﴾. Al-Sadiq said: "Your bodies have no price except Paradise, so do not sell them except for it."

﴿The repentant﴾ is in the nominative (*raf'*) by way of praise (*madh*), meaning: they are the repentant, that is, the believers already mentioned. Or it is a subject (*mubtada'*) whose predicate (*khabar*) is ﴿the worshippers﴾, meaning: those who worshipped God alone and devoted worship sincerely to Him. What follows is a predicate after a predicate, meaning: the truly repentant from disbelief, who combine these qualities. It is narrated from al-Hasan: they are those who repented from polytheism and disowned hypocrisy. ﴿The praisers﴾ are those who praise Him for the blessing of Islam. ﴿The wanderers﴾ are the fasting ones, based on his saying ﷺ: "The wandering of my community is fasting." Or they are seekers of knowledge, because they travel the earth seeking it in its sources. Or they are those who travel the earth for contemplation. ﴿The bowers and the prostrators﴾ are those who keep to the prayers. ﴿Those who enjoin what is right﴾ do so with faith, knowledge and obedience. ﴿And those who forbid what is wrong﴾ forbid polytheism and sins. The conjunction *wa* (and) is used to indicate that the seven form a complete set, or to show the contrast between the command and the prohibition, as in His saying: ﴿thayyibat wa-abkaran (previously married and virgin)﴾ [al-Tahrim: 5]. ﴿And those who guard the limits of God﴾ are those who keep His commands and prohibitions, or the markers of the Sharia. ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾ who possess these qualities.

The Prophet (ﷺ) intended to seek forgiveness for Abu Talib, and then this was revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to seek forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were close relatives﴾. That is: it was not proper for him to seek forgiveness, according to the judgment of Allah and His wisdom, ﴿after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire﴾, after it has become evident to them that they died in polytheism. Then he mentioned the excuse of Ibrahim, and said:

That is, his father promised him that he would embrace Islam. Or it was he who promised his father that he would ask forgiveness for him, which is his saying: ﴿I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾ (al-Mumtahanah 60:4). Its evidence is the reading of al-Hasan: ﴿and he had promised it to him﴾. The meaning of his asking forgiveness is his request for forgiveness for him after he had embraced Islam, or his request that he be granted Islam, through which he would be forgiven. ﴿So when it became clear﴾ to Abraham, through revelation, ﴿to him﴾, ﴿that he﴾, that his father, ﴿was an enemy of Allah﴾, who would die as a disbeliever, his hope for him was cut off.

﴿He disassociated himself from him﴾ and ended his request for forgiveness. ﴿Indeed, Abraham (p-٧١٤) was ʾawwāh﴾, meaning one who sighs (yata'awwahu) out of compassion and fear. Its meaning is that, because of the abundance of his tenderness and softness of heart, he would show kindness toward his disbelieving father. ﴿Forbearing﴾: he is patient in the face of trials and forgiving of harm, because he used to ask forgiveness for his father, while the latter was saying: "I will surely stone you."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 115:

﴿And Allah would never mislead a people after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should fear (avoid).﴾ That is: what Allah has not commanded them to guard against and avoid, such as seeking forgiveness for the polytheists, and other things He has forbidden, and He has made clear that they are prohibited. He does not hold His servants accountable for them, those whom He has guided to Islam, nor does He forsake them, except when they come before Him after the clarification of their prohibition and their knowledge that it is obligatory to comply with it. As for before knowledge and clarification, then no. This is an explanation of the excuse of one who feared being held accountable for seeking forgiveness for the polytheists. The meaning of ﴿what they should fear﴾ is what must be guarded against due to a prohibition; as for what is known by reason (ʿaql), it is not dependent on revelation (tawqīf) ﴿that Allah is Knowing of all things﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 116–117:

﴿Indeed, Allah turned in mercy to the Prophet﴾. That is: Allah turned to him (accepted his repentance) for his permission granted to the hypocrites to stay behind from him, like His saying: ﴿Allah pardon you. Why did you give them permission?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 43]. ﴿And the Muhajirun and the Ansar﴾. In this there is an incitement for the believers to repentance, and that there is no believer except that he is in need of repentance and seeking forgiveness, even the Prophet ﷺ, and the Muhajirun and the Ansar, ﴿who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾ in the expedition of Tabuk. Its meaning: in its time. The word "sa'ah" (hour) is used in the sense of unrestricted time. They were in hardship regarding the mount: ten would take turns riding a single camel. As for the provisions, they took along dates that were full of worms, barley that was infested with weevils, and rancid ghee. Their distress reached the point (p-715) that two people would share a single date, and sometimes a group would suck on it so that they could drink water after it. As for the water, [their distress reached the point] that they slaughtered the camels and squeezed out their stomach contents and drank them, in a time of severe heat of the summer and of drought and famine. ﴿After the hearts of a faction of them had nearly swerved﴾ from steadfastness in faith, or from following the Messenger in that expedition and going out with him. In "kada" (nearly) there is a pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-sha'n), and the clause after it is in the accusative position, and it is like their saying: "Allah's creation is not like Him," meaning: the matter is not that Allah's creation is like Him. ("Yazigh") is recited by Hamzah and Hafs.

﴿Then He turned to them in mercy﴾: a repetition for emphasis. ﴿Indeed, He is toward them Kind and Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 116–117:

﴿Indeed, Allah turned in mercy to the Prophet﴾. That is: Allah turned to him (accepted his repentance) for his permission granted to the hypocrites to stay behind from him, like His saying: ﴿Allah pardon you. Why did you give them permission?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 43]. ﴿And the Muhajirun and the Ansar﴾. In this there is an incitement for the believers to repentance, and that there is no believer except that he is in need of repentance and seeking forgiveness, even the Prophet ﷺ, and the Muhajirun and the Ansar, ﴿who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾ in the expedition of Tabuk. Its meaning: in its time. The word "sa'ah" (hour) is used in the sense of unrestricted time. They were in hardship regarding the mount: ten would take turns riding a single camel. As for the provisions, they took along dates that were full of worms, barley that was infested with weevils, and rancid ghee. Their distress reached the point (p-715) that two people would share a single date, and sometimes a group would suck on it so that they could drink water after it. As for the water, [their distress reached the point] that they slaughtered the camels and squeezed out their stomach contents and drank them, in a time of severe heat of the summer and of drought and famine. ﴿After the hearts of a faction of them had nearly swerved﴾ from steadfastness in faith, or from following the Messenger in that expedition and going out with him. In "kada" (nearly) there is a pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-sha'n), and the clause after it is in the accusative position, and it is like their saying: "Allah's creation is not like Him," meaning: the matter is not that Allah's creation is like Him. ("Yazigh") is recited by Hamzah and Hafs.

﴿Then He turned to them in mercy﴾: a repetition for emphasis. ﴿Indeed, He is toward them Kind and Merciful﴾.

﴿And to the three﴾, meaning: "and" He relented ("tāba") toward the three. This is an ʿaṭf (conjunction, grammatically linked) to [His turning toward] the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿who were left behind﴾ from the expedition, ﴿until, when the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness﴾, that is, despite its expanse. This is a metaphor for their bewilderment in their affair, as if they could find no place in it where they could settle, from anxiety and distress.

﴿And their souls became constricted for them﴾, meaning their hearts could contain neither comfort nor joy, because they had departed from them out of extreme estrangement and grief. ﴿And they thought that there was no refuge from Allah except in Him﴾, and they knew that there was no refuge from the wrath of Allah except in seeking His forgiveness. ﴿Then He relented toward them﴾ after fifty days, ﴿that they might repent﴾, so that they would be among those who repent often. ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful.﴾

It is related from Abū Bakr al-Warrāq that he said: "Sincere repentance (al-tawbah al-naṣūḥ) is that the earth becomes constricted for the one repenting despite its vastness, and his own soul becomes constricted for him, as with the repentance of these three."

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with those who are truthful.﴾ (i.e., truthful in their faith, as opposed to the hypocrites); or, with those who did not stay behind; or, with those who were truthful in their religion of Allah in intention, speech, and action. The verse indicates that consensus (ijma') is a proof (hujjah), because He commanded being with the truthful, so it is obligatory to accept their word.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on Surah 9, verse 120:**

﴿It was not for the people of Medina and those of the Bedouins around them to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah.﴾ The purpose of this negation is a prohibition (*nahy*).

These people were singled out for mention, although all people are equal in this matter, because of their proximity to him, and his departure is not hidden from them.

﴿Nor to care more﴾ and not to hold back ﴿their own selves from his self﴾, meaning from what befalls his self. That is, they should not choose to preserve themselves over him in hardships. Rather, they were commanded to accompany him in adversity and affliction, and to cast themselves before him in every severe situation. ﴿That﴾ prohibition against remaining behind is ﴿because they﴾ are such that ﴿no thirst afflicts them﴾, meaning thirst, ﴿nor fatigue﴾, meaning exhaustion, ﴿nor hunger﴾, meaning starvation, ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, meaning in jihad, ﴿nor do they tread on a place﴾, meaning they do not step on any place of the unbelievers with the hooves of their horses, the hoofs of their mounts, or their feet.

﴿That enrages the unbelievers﴾, meaning it angers them and constricts their hearts.

﴿Nor do they inflict on an enemy any harm﴾, meaning they do not inflict on them any harm, whether by killing, capture, wounding, breaking, or defeat.

﴿But a righteous deed is recorded for them thereby.﴾ It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "For every moment of terror, there are seventy thousand good deeds." It is said: "He inflicted harm upon him" when he diminished or reduced him. This is general in regard to everything that displeases them. In this there is evidence that whoever intends good, his striving in it is rewarded, whether by standing, sitting, walking, speaking, or other things. It also shows that a reinforcement (*madad*) shares in the spoils with the army after the war has ended, because trampling their lands is among the things that enrages them. The Prophet (ﷺ) assigned a share to the two sons of ʿAmir, although they arrived after the war had ended.

As for *al-mawṭiʾ* (the place of treading), it is either a verbal noun (*maṣdar*, the infinitive form of the verb) like *al-mawrid*, or it is a place. If it is a place, then the meaning of "it enrages the unbelievers" is that their being trodden upon enrages them. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost﴾, meaning: they are doers of good, and Allah does not nullify their reward.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 121:

﴿And they spend no expenditure﴾ in the way of Allah, ﴿small﴾, even if it is a date, ﴿nor large﴾, like what ʿUthman (may Allah be pleased with him) spent in the army of hardship (jaysh al-ʿusrah). ﴿Nor do they cross a valley﴾, that is: a land, in their going and coming. It is every opening between mountains and hills that serves as a passage for the torrent (sayl). Originally it is an active participle (fāʿil), from wada, meaning "to flow" when water runs. From it comes al-wadi (the valley). It has become common in usage with the meaning of land,

﴿except that it is written for them﴾ of the spending and the crossing of the valley.

﴿that Allah may reward them﴾ is connected to "was written", that is: it is recorded in their scrolls for the purpose of recompense ﴿for the best of what they used to do﴾, that is: He rewards them for each single act with the reward of the best deed they performed, so that what is less than it is joined to it, multiplying their reward.

The Believers should not all go forth [to war]. The lam here is for emphasis of the negation: that it is not correct for all of them to leave their homelands to seek knowledge, since that would lead to corruption. ﴿Why should there not go forth﴾ — so, since it is not the case that all go forth, ﴿from every division of them a party﴾ — that is, from every large group, a small group of them, who will suffice for them in going forth. ﴿That they may gain understanding in the religion﴾ — that they may take upon themselves the effort of acquiring fiqh (deep understanding) of it, and endure hardships in attaining it. ﴿And that they may warn their people﴾ — and that they may make the aim of their resolve in seeking understanding the warning and guidance of their people, ﴿when they return to them﴾ — rather than base worldly aims such as seeking prominence, leadership, and imitating the oppressors in their mounts and clothing. ﴿That they may beware﴾ — of what must be avoided.

It has been said that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dispatched an expedition after the Battle of Tabuk, following the revelation of the severe verses concerning those who stayed behind, all the Believers, to a man, rushed forth to go out, and all of them ceased from gaining understanding in the religion. So they were commanded that from every division of them a party should go forth to jihad, while the rest remain to gain understanding, so that they would not be cut off from the understanding which is the greater jihad, since jihad by argument has a greater effect than jihad by combat. The pronoun in "li-yatafaqqahu" (that they may gain understanding) refers to the remaining divisions after the going-forth parties from among them.

﴿And that they may warn their people﴾ — and the remaining divisions should warn their people, those who went forth, when they return to them, with the knowledge they acquired during their absence. On the first view, the pronoun refers to the party that went forth to Madinah for the purpose of gaining understanding.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 123:

﴿O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers﴾ who are close to you. ﴿Fighting is obligatory with all the disbelievers, near and far, but the nearer are more obligatory [to fight] than the nearer.﴾ The Prophet (ﷺ) fought his own people, then other Arabs of the Hijaz, then the Levant (al-Sham), and al-Sham is closer to Madinah than Iraq and others. Likewise, it is obligatory upon the people of every region to fight those who are adjacent to them. ﴿And let them find in you harshness﴾ severity and roughness in speech before the fighting.

﴿And know that Allah is with the righteous﴾ with victory and triumph.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 124:

﴿And when a surah is sent down﴾ — "mā" is a superfluous particle (ṣila) serving for emphasis. ﴿Among them﴾ — that is, among the hypocrites (al-munāfiqīn). ﴿Is one who says﴾ — some of them saying to others: ﴿"Which of you has had his faith increased by this"﴾ surah? — as a denial and as mockery of the believers. And "ayyukum" (which of you) is in the nominative case as the subject of a nominal sentence (mubtada'). It was said:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 125:

﴿As for those in whose hearts is a sickness﴾: doubt and hypocrisy. It is a corruption that requires a cure, like corruption in the body.

﴿it adds to them uncleanness on top of their uncleanness﴾: they disbelieved, with disbelief added to their disbelief. ﴿And they die while they are disbelievers﴾: this is a report of their persistence in it until death.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 126:

﴿Do they not see?﴾ That is, the hypocrites. With the (ta') reading, Hamzah [reads it as addressing the believers]: an address to the believers. ﴿That they are tested﴾ are being afflicted with drought, sickness, and other [calamities] ﴿every year, once or twice, yet they do not repent﴾ from their hypocrisy ﴿nor do they take heed﴾, that is, they do not learn a lesson. Or, [it means] ﴿they do not repent﴾ through jihad alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), despite what they see of the rise of the state of Islam,

﴿nor do they take heed﴾ from what befalls them of collisions.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 127:

﴿And when a surah is revealed, they look at one another, [saying]: "Does anyone see you?"﴾ They signalled to one another with their eyes, denying the revelation and mocking it, saying: ﴿Does anyone see you?﴾ — [i.e., of] the Muslims — "so that we may slip away, for we cannot endure listening to it, and laughter overcomes us, and we fear being disgraced among them." Or [the meaning is]: when a surah is revealed concerning the faults of the hypocrites, some of them signalled to others: ﴿Does anyone see you?﴾ — if you stand up from his presence ﷺ. ﴿Then they turn away﴾ from the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, fearing exposure. ﴿God has turned their hearts﴾ away from understanding the Qur'an ﴿because they﴾ — because they are ﴿a people who do not understand﴾, that is, they do not reflect so as to comprehend.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 128:

﴿Indeed there has come to you a Messenger﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿from among yourselves﴾ from your own kind and from your lineage: an Arab, a Qurashi like yourselves.

﴿Grievous to him is what you suffer﴾ it is difficult and burdensome for him, because he is a part of you, that you suffer hardship and encounter what is disliked, so he fears for you falling into punishment. ﴿He is eager for you﴾ for your faith ﴿and to the believers﴾ among you and among others ﴿kind and merciful﴾. It was said: Allah did not combine two of His names for anyone other than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿Then if they turn away﴾ — that is, if they turn away from believing in you and oppose you. ﴿Say: Allah is sufficient for me﴾ — so seek help from Allah and entrust your affairs to Him; He is sufficient for you against their harm and is your helper against them.

﴿There is no god but Him. In Him I have put my trust﴾ — I have entrusted my affair to Him. ﴿And He is the Lord of the Throne﴾ — it is the greatest of Allah's creation; it was created as a place of circumambulation for the people of the heavens and a qibla for supplication. ﴿The Mighty﴾ — read with the kasra (genitive, jarr), as an epithet of "the Throne." It is also read with the damma (raf'), as an epithet of the Lord, exalted and glorified is He.

On the authority of Ubayy (ibn Ka'b): the last verse revealed was ﴿Indeed there has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128] — the verse.
